body.statement: Uniformly over every deterministic binary schedule \(Y\) satisfying the stated design and stratified-interference conditions, \[\Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\left\{\mathcal O(N^\star)\in\widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\right\}\ge 1-\alpha.\] The covered object is the complete weak order, so the assertion simultaneously covers all policy ranks, every partial tie pattern, and every zero-variance face. No pairwise allocation of \(\alpha\) and no cross-arm covariance estimator enters the construction. As an immediate reporting corollary, for each \(r\in\mathcal R\), take the union of the integer positions occupied by \(r\) over the retained weak orders, letting a tied block contribute every position that it spans. With the same probability, these rank sets simultaneously contain every policy's true tied-rank interval.
body.justification: This theorem supplies the finite-sample simultaneous coverage guarantee for the causal weak order under the exact two-stage design.
body.gap: Existing generic rank methods require a simultaneous difference region, while nearby exact interference procedures target scalar or more sharply restricted nulls rather than the complete weak order of average quota-policy welfare.
body.consumer: RCT2 and the Baird--Bohren--McIntosh--Özler design calculator can report complete and tied policy orderings that remain compatible at level \(1-\alpha\).
body.proof_tex:
Fix a deterministic binary schedule \(Y\).  For a cluster \(c\) of response type \(t_c^\star=t\) and a policy \(r\), exact second-stage randomization gives
\[
 \Pr(Z_{ci}=1\mid R_c=r)=\frac{k_r}{n}
 \qquad(i\in\mathcal I),
\]
because each of the \(\binom n{k_r}\) subsets is equally likely and \(\binom{n-1}{k_r-1}/\binom n{k_r}=k_r/n\).  Fixed potential outcomes and stratified interference therefore imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 W_{cr}
 &:=\mathbb E_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\!\left[
      \frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}Y_{ci}(Z_{ci},r)
      \;\middle|\;R_c=r\right]\\
 &=\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}
   \left\{\left(1-\frac{k_r}{n}\right)Y_{ci}(0,r)
          +\frac{k_r}{n}Y_{ci}(1,r)\right\}\\
 &=\frac{(n-k_r)(N_{c,r}^{10}+N_{c,r}^{11})
          +k_r(N_{c,r}^{01}+N_{c,r}^{11})}{n^2}
 =u_{t_c^\star r}=u_{tr}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The conditioning event has positive probability because \(m_r\ge1\) and the uniform exact first stage gives \(\Pr(R_c=r)=m_r/C>0\).  The displayed expression is the design-average outcome under the intervention that assigns quota policy \(r\) to cluster \(c\), and the interior-quota condition ensures every unit has both own-treatment states in the second-stage support.  Averaging over the fixed clusters and grouping equal response types yields
\[
 \frac1C\sum_{c\in\mathcal C}W_{cr}
 =\frac1C\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}N_t^\star u_{tr}
 =U_r(N^\star).
\]
Thus \(\mathcal O(N^\star)\) is the complete weak order of fixed finite-population causal policy welfares.  The empirical vector \(\widehat U(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\) is only a randomization statistic and is not being identified with that causal vector.

By \(\texttt{lem:true-counts-compatible}\),
\(N^\star\in\mathcal N(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\) for every realization.  Hence the definition of the confidence set gives
\[
 \{p_{N^\star}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})>\alpha\}
 \subseteq
 \{\mathcal O(N^\star)\in
       \widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\}.
\]
Taking complements and applying \(\texttt{lem:schedule-pvalue-valid}\) with \(N=N^\star\) and \(q=\alpha\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\!\left\{
   \mathcal O(N^\star)\notin
   \widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})
 \right\}
 &\le
 \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\!\left\{
   p_{N^\star}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\le\alpha
 \right\}\\
 &\le\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\]
This argument is pointwise in \(Y\), so the lower coverage bound is uniform over all schedules satisfying the four stated assumptions.  The cited super-uniformity result already permits discrete and degenerate randomization distributions; consequently no continuity, positive-variance, rank, or limiting condition is used.

For the reporting corollary, represent a retained weak order as descending tied blocks \((B_1,\ldots,B_J)\).  If \(r\in B_j\), define its occupied-position interval by
\[
 \rho_{\mathcal O}(r)
 =\left\{1+\sum_{\ell<j}|B_\ell|,\ldots,
              \sum_{\ell\le j}|B_\ell|\right\}.
\]
On the coverage event the true weak order is retained, and therefore, simultaneously for every \(r\in\mathcal R\),
\[
 \rho_{\mathcal O(N^\star)}(r)
 \subseteq
 \bigcup_{\mathcal O\in
   \widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})}
 \rho_{\mathcal O}(r).
\]
This is precisely simultaneous containment of all true tied-rank intervals.
